parsed.summary: The paper introduces A LBIREO, an adaptive, detector-agnostic, and codec-free frame-skipping framework designed to improve the energy efficiency of video object detection on edge devices. By utilizing a Kalman filter uncertainty trigger, a detector-flicker rescue mechanism, and an empty-scene screen, the system decides when detector invocations can be safely skipped. Evaluation on the BDD100K dataset shows that A LBIREO reduces total energy consumption by 12.1–17.6% while keeping detection accuracy within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference.

chk_problem.value: High energy consumption and sustained GPU utilization of running computationally expensive video object detectors on edge devices.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Video object detection on edge devices requires running computationally expensive detectors over long frame streams, leading to high energy consumption and sustained GPU utilization.

chk_method.value: A LBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free adaptive inference framework that uses Kalman filter uncertainty, detector-flicker rescue, and empty-scene screening to skip redundant detector calls.
chk_method.paper_quote: We present A LBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework that wraps off-the-shelf object detectors and decides when detector invocation can be safely skipped based on scene content and per-object temporal state.

chk_data.value: The BDD100K dataset's multi-object tracking (MOT) validation split, consisting of 200 dashcam clips and 7 object classes.
chk_data.paper_quote: We evaluate A LBIREO on the BDD100K dataset’s multiobject tracking (MOT) validation split using three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large) on two NVIDIA Jetson platforms (AGX Thor and AGX Orin).

chk_setup.value: Evaluating three distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, RF-DETR-Large) on two NVIDIA Jetson platforms (AGX Thor and AGX Orin).
chk_setup.paper_quote: We evaluate A LBIREO on the BDD100K dataset’s multiobject tracking (MOT) validation split using three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large) on two NVIDIA Jetson platforms (AGX Thor and AGX Orin).

chk_primary_result.value: A LBIREO keeps AP@50 within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference while reducing total energy by 12.1–17.6% across all configurations.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Across all detector–platform configurations, A LBIREO keeps AP@50 (average precision at IoU 0.5) within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference while reducing total energy by 12.1–17.6%.

chk_secondary_result.value: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, A LBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor and 14.4% on Orin.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, A LBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor and 14.4% on Orin.

chk_baseline.value: Compared against five families of frame-skipping baselines, including Vanilla per-frame inference, FixedSkip-N, Confidence-Triggered Detection (CTD), Statues, and ERD-only.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: We compare A LBIREO against five families of frame-skipping baselines.

chk_conclusion.value: Using object-level temporal state via A LBIREO serves as a practical drop-in efficiency layer for off-the-shelf edge video detection pipelines.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: These results show that using the object-level temporal state can serve as a practical drop-in efficiency layer for off-the-shelf edge video detection pipelines.

chk_limitation.value: The constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics can drift under highly erratic motion, such as a pedestrian making an abrupt lateral move.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: First, the constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics fit many vehicle-dominated dashcam scenes, but can drift under highly erratic motion, such as a pedestrian making an abrupt lateral move at a crosswalk.
